entry.title: Japan and the Philippines Narrow Their Destroyer Talks to a First Ship
entry.summary: An Oct. 28 joint statement turns the Abukuma-class talks toward a first ship and puts Japanese training support before any transfer. Neither language version records a transfer decision.

entry.title: Japan and the United States Agree to Establish AMRAAM Final Assembly in Japan
entry.summary: In April the allies agreed only to keep discussing final assembly in Japan; in October their defense ministers committed to it. They also agreed to share technical information for SM-3 Block IIA production, though neither government's public account names a site, operator, contract or production rate.

entry.title: Bersama Lima 2026 Tests Five-Power Coordination at Sea
entry.summary: A New Zealand boarding team operated from a British patrol ship amid a wider multinational exercise. Public accounts reveal the tasks attempted—not whether the forces performed better together.

entry.title: Three Days of Chinese Flights, Six Months of Japanese Scrambles
entry.summary: Japan's October air reports capture repeated Y-9 flights near its southwestern approaches. Newly released scramble figures give those encounters a longer—and more revealing—context.

entry.title: What Is Being Built in Laos?
entry.summary: Vietnam’s digital-identity handover and China’s military training center reveal different kinds of cooperation—and how little a completed project necessarily tells us about enduring influence.
